summary.title: Physically Based Rendering: From Theory to Implementation
summary.one_liner: A textbook on the math and implementation of physically based photorealistic rendering, presented with literate programming so the explanations and source code appear together.
keywords: how do i write a path tracer
takeaways: Physically based rendering models the physics of light scattering to produce photorealistic images.
The book pairs the mathematical theory of a modern rendering system with its practical implementation.
Literate programming combines documentation and source code into one reference.
The book covers newer material such as GPU ray tracing.
The full contents of the third and fourth editions are freely available online.
summary.summary: The page presents Physically Based Rendering, a computer graphics textbook by Matt Pharr, Greg Humphreys, and Pat Hanrahan, now in a fourth edition. It describes the mathematical theory behind a modern photorealistic rendering system alongside its implementation, using literate programming to merge prose and source code. The page notes the book's 2014 Academy Award recognition for its influence on film production and that the third and fourth editions are freely available online. The listing places it under C++ for building a 3D renderer.
